1.q: to the right of the altar
1.note: This is the right side of the altar when a person looks at it while they are facing east, so it is on the south side of the altar. Alternate translation: [on the south side of the altar]

2.note: Alternate translation: [the eastern gate] or [the eastern gate of the outer wall]

3.note: a string or a rope that people use to measure longer distances
Each long cubit was about 54 centimeters. Alternate translation: [1,000 cubits] or [about 540 meters]

5.q: a river that could not be crossed
5.note: This can be translated in active form. Alternate translation: [a river that no one could cross on foot]

6.note: God calls Ezekiel this to emphasize that Ezekiel is only a human being. God is eternal and powerful, but humans are not. See how you translated this in [Ezekiel 2:1](ta:02). Alternate translation: [Mortal person] or [Human]
Yahweh is commanding Ezekiel to think about what he has just seen. See how you translated this in Ezekiel 8:15. Alternate translation: [think about this.]

9.note: The phrase **the two streams** is a translation of the standard written Hebrew text as we have it today. This could refer to this new stream from the temple along with the existing Jordan River, which currently flows into the Dead Sea, or it could be referring to this one stream with the dual form because sacred rivers may have been thought of as having two flows. You may want to follow an alternative reading from the ancient Greek translation, however, which simply says, “the stream” or you may want to follow the major translation in your area. Alternate translation: [the stream comes]

10.note: See how you translated this in Ezekiel 21:7.
This is the name of a very large spring on the western side of the Salt Sea.

10.q: a place to dry out the fishing nets
10.note: Alternate translation: [a place for people to dry out their fishing nets]
This is the name of a large spring on the eastern side of the Salt Sea.

11.note: places with shallow water and trees growing in deep mud
places with shallow water and grasses growing in deep mud

13.note: The person is a metonym for his descendants. Alternate translation: [the descendants of Joseph will receive two areas of land]

14.q: I lifted up my hand and swore
14.note: In those days a person would raise his right hand to show that he realized that God would punish him if he did not do what he swore to do.

These are the names of towns.

18.note: This is the name of a town.

The phrase **you shall measure** is a translation of the standard written Hebrew text as we have it today. The translator of the ancient Greek translation, however, read a similar word that means, “to Tamar,” a town south of the Salt Sea. You may want to follow this alternative reading from the ancient Greek translation, or you may want to follow the major translation in your area. Alternate translation: [to Tamar]
